title: What is known about 1RB0RE_0RC1RE_1RD1LE_0LE---_1RA1LF_1RF0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_0RC1RE_1RD1LE_0LE---_1RA1LF_1RF0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is the alternating pattern 0101... broken by a few domain walls (two equal neighbours, 00 or 11). E and A flip whole domains as they cross them (proved in Lean). In samples to 3·108 steps the number of walls stays between 12 and 14 while the tape grows to 48,000 cells. How walls move, appear and annihilate is not worked out, so halting (D reading a 1) is not ruled out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 85,057 cells have been visited and 42,524 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 5.10×10<sup>18</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 5,108,939,772,420,755,088 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,015,467 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.596). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.237).

claims.title: Crossing domains
claims.text: E> (01)^n → (10)^n E> and A> (10)^n → (01)^n A>, for every n.

claims.title: A dozen walls
claims.text: At every 300th visit of F to the left end, from step 2.45·10<sup>8</sup> to 3·10<sup>8</sup>, the tape (41,000 to 48,000 cells) has 12 to 14 places where two neighbouring cells are equal.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when D reads a 1. D is entered from C on a 0 (writing 1, moving right), next to a wall. A halt needs a wall shape or a pair of walls closer than any seen. The walls' dynamics is not known. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LC_0LC---_1RE1LD_1RD0LA_1RF0RC_0RA1RC up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1LF_1RC0RA_0RD1RA_1RE1LA_0LA---_1RF0LD up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: E and A crossing domains, flipping their phase.
No halt in the C simulator; 85,057 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Domains and walls
html: Every domain is the period-2 pattern. Where (01) meets (10) there are two equal cells, a wall. A sweep to the right flips each domain it crosses, 01 ↔ 10, in one go (proved in Lean for E and A). The walls are where the head turns, and each sweep shifts some walls by a cell or two.

sections.heading: Walls that move
html:
The tape grows (sqrt-like on the left, a smaller power on the right), but the number of walls does not: 12 to 14 in the samples between 2.45·108 and 3·108 steps. So the domains keep getting longer. Their lengths (2,426, 1,439, 206, 1,894, 50, ...) look irregular, like a small system of particles moving at different speeds that is fed new particles at the ends.

What halting would need. D reading a 1, which would take an unusual wall or two walls very close together. Proving non-halting would mean classifying the walls and their collisions. A CTL over the alphabet {01, 10, wall types} could be a way in.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.596). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.237).
After 109 steps the tape spans 85,057 cells (65,150 left of the start, 105 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Domains of the pairs 01 and 10 separated by about a dozen domain walls (00 or 11); sweeps flip the phase of every domain and move the walls, so the domains grow while the number of walls stays near 13; the domain lengths look irregular.
family: domain walls in a period-2 background
